title: Hybrid Fidelity Contract Anchors and Migration Playbook
content:
summary: >
  This playbook defines product, pricing and technical requirements for "Hybrid Fidelity" commercial bundles (a combined hosted/dedicated/private fidelity contract model), the contract-anchor concept, migration patterns for existing customers, and the operational runbook for rolling out the SKU set. It spans product overview, PRD-style acceptance criteria, design-level integration notes, roadmap milestones, pricing examples and release notes.

## Context and high-level goal

Redwood offers multiple ways to trade cost and latency vs. output fidelity. Customers need clear contract constructs and migration paths when moving between Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments while preserving SLAs and predictable billing. The Hybrid Fidelity Contract Anchors product provides:

- A small set of auditable contract "anchors" that define fidelity bands (Platinum, Gold, Silver) mapped to model families, quantization profiles, and routing policies.
- A migration assistant + billing adapter to transition existing customers onto anchor-based SKUs with minimal invoicing noise.
- A runtime coordination layer (fidelity-orchestrator) that enforces routing, fallback economics, and fidelity fallthrough rules.

Audience: Product managers, commercial leads (GTM), billing/finance, engineering (runtime, billing-bridge, console), customer success.

## Scope

In-scope:
- Definition of fidelity anchors and the canonical SKU mapping.
- PRD acceptance criteria for the migration assistant and billing adapter.
- Design constraints for the fidelity-orchestrator and runtime enforcement hooks.
- Roadmap for a staged roll-out and commercial experiments.

Out-of-scope:
- New model training or model variant creation.
- Deep changes to existing legal contract terms (requires legal team separate engagement).

## Product requirements (PRD style)

Goals:
1. Customers can buy a single contract (anchor) which guarantees a fidelity band across deployments.
2. Transitioning customers must see <= 3% variance on monthly spend (estimate) during migration under typical traffic patterns.
3. Runtime must enforce fidelity contracts with observable fallbacks and per-request auditability.

Key user stories:
- As a Developer, I can select a fidelity anchor on my account and immediately see an estimate of expected latency and monthly cost.
- As an SRE, I can query per-route fidelity decisions and upstream fallback decisions for debugging.
- As a Finance lead, I can reconcile pre- and post-migration invoices using the migration adapter CSV and mapping table.

Acceptance criteria (must pass):
- UI: Console shows anchor selection with estimated 95th percentile latency and monthly spend range.
- API: admin API to set anchor per-tenant returns 200 and an audit entry (event: anchor.changed).
- Billing: Adapter generates mapping file and invoice adjustments for first billing cycle with delta explanation notes.
- Runtime: fidelity-orchestrator logs every cross-variant fallback with reason, matched SLA tag, and cost-delta estimate in telemetry.

## Non-functional requirements

- Latency overhead: fidelity-orchestrator decision path must add < 2ms p50 to request path in hosted mode, < 5ms p50 in private deployments.
- Availability: anchor decision service SLA 99.95% across regions.
- Observability: 100% sampling of anchor change events; 1% sampling of per-request decision traces by default (configurable).

## Design summary (high level)

Components:
- fidelity-orchestrator (service): maps anchor -> runtime policy (preferred model group, allowed quantization levels, routing priority).
- billing-bridge (service): consumes tenant->anchor assignments and emits SKU mapping and billable adjustments.
- console (UI): anchor selector and migration assistant flow.
- migration-assistant (batch + streaming): runs a simulation of expected spend and generates a recommended anchor per tenant.

Key contracts and APIs (examples):
- POST /admin/v1/tenants/{id}/anchor { "anchor": "platinum-v2" } => 200
- GET /admin/v1/tenants/{id}/anchor/logs => list of audit events
- Webhook: /billing/v1/anchor-mappings (billing-bridge) accepts anchor -> sku diff payloads

Runtime enforcement rules (summary):
1. Prefer models in the anchor's whitelist. If capacity unavailable, fallback to anchor-compatible variants following priority list.
2. On fallback, emit telemetry: event.fallback{tenant, route, from_model, to_model, reason, estimated_cost_delta}
3. If fallback leads to > 20% cost delta for the tenant's billing period, trigger an alert to customer-success and billing teams.

Compatibility and limits:
- Anchors are compatible with existing per-route SLOs and can be scoped per-tenant or per-route (tenant-level default with route overrides).
- Migration assistant will warn when historical quantization usage suggests >10% quality risk; those tenants require manual approval.

## Pricing & packaging model

Anchor tiers (canonical):

| Anchor | Model families (preferred) | Typical latency band (p95) | Billing approach |
|--------|----------------------------|----------------------------|------------------|
| Platinum | stateful-opt, large-open | 60–120ms | Higher per-token + fidelity premium, reserved burst capacity included |
| Gold     | balanced-latency, quant-friendly | 80–180ms | Mid per-token with optional reserved pool add-on |
| Silver   | cost-optimized, strong quant | 120–350ms | Lower per-token; preemptible capacity for non-critical workloads |

Pricing rules (examples):
- Base per-token rate derived from model family + quantization multiplier.
- Anchor premium: fixed % uplift for Platinum (e.g., +25%) applied to baseline compute tokens.
- Reserved capacity credits: bundled with Platinum and optionally Gold; redeemed against actual usage.
- Migration credit: first month credit to neutralize invoice delta up to $X or 5% of monthly committed spend (whichever smaller).

Billing edge cases:
- If a tenant is routed to fallback models outside anchor compatibility due to blackout, billing-bridge emits a flagged line item labeled "emergency-fallback" and flags finance reconciliation.

## Migration playbook (step-by-step)

1. Run migration-assistant in simulation mode to profile 30 days of traffic and produce recommended anchor and expected monthly spend delta.
2. Present recommendation to customer via CS portal with toggles: Accept, Request manual review, or Delay.
3. On Accept: schedule a low-risk migration window (24–72h) during low traffic; enable anchor in dry-run (no billing) for 48h and collect telemetry.
4. If dry-run meets quality thresholds (see QA criteria), flip to active anchor and trigger billing adapter for SKU mapping.
5. Monitor first 7-day delta window; if spend delta > 10% or quality regression detected, run rollback steps and open postmortem.

Rollback steps (quick):
1. Disable anchor at tenant level via admin API.
2. Re-apply previous routing policy and inform billing to pause any invoice adjustments.
3. Create incident with engineering + CS to triage cause (model supply vs quantization mismatch).

QA Criteria (must be met during dry-run):
- Latency: p95 within anchor predicted band ±15%.
- Quality: shadow-eval metric (WER/semantic-similarity) within threshold defined per-customer promptset (default: ≤ 3% degradation).
- Cost: projected monthly spend delta ≤ 5%.

## Roadmap / milestones

- Q1: Design sign-off, API contracts, console mockups, legal review on migration credit language.
- Q2: Implementation: fidelity-orchestrator MVP, migration-assistant v1, billing-bridge adapter prototype.
- Q3: Pilot with 5 anchor customers, collect telemetry, iterate pricing heuristics.
- Q4: GA launch with console anchor picker, billing automation, and GTM package.

Metrics to track:
- Anchor adoption rate (% of active tenants with anchors assigned).
- Migration delta percent (median, 90th percentile) across pilots.
- Number of emergency-fallback events per 1M requests.
- CS satisfaction score post migration (NPS change).

## Release notes (first release)

Release: Hybrid Fidelity Anchors — Pilot 1
Date: 2030-01-07
Highlights:
- Introduced anchor selection on Console (beta) and admin API for tenant assignment.
- fidelity-orchestrator enforces anchor whitelist with telemetry for every fallback.
- migration-assistant generates recommended anchor and simulated billing delta report.
- billing-bridge emits anchor -> SKU mapping files and a one-time migration credit in the pilot flow.
Known limitations:
- Private deployments require an op-approval for anchor enforcement during pilot (no automatic billing adapter in on-premises air-gapped sites).
- Per-route override UX is limited to API during pilot (console support planned in Q3).

## Operational runbook (short)

Immediate alerts to create:
- Anchor-change-failure (if admin API returns 5xx)
- Emergency-fallback-rate > 0.1% sustained over 30m for a tenant
- Migration-delta > 10% in initial billing cycle

Escalation paths and pager rotations are defined in the eng-platform runbook (see related pages).

Appendix: sample CLI for dry-run simulation

redwood migrate simulate --tenant tenant_abc --window 30d --output report.json

CLI output fields (report.json):
- recommended_anchor
- estimated_monthly_spend
- expected_latency_profile
- flagged_quality_risks
